reviews.title: Good app,  but wish it were better
reviews.text:
I am a perimenopausal working mom with ADHD, so I NEED something like this to help me be productive throughout the day and remember things and be my “second brain.”

Overall I really like the app (so much that I got the lifetime subscription), but there are two minor complaints I have when using it. When I add things to my day in the morning, afternoon, or evening blocks, I wish it was easier to drag to reorder the things I need to get done in order of priority or somewhat chronological order without assigning set times to them. I’m not sure if it’s just my app being glitchy, but every time I move one task and then try to move another, it resets everything or puts things in a weird order that I did not want. The other one is the “AI assistant” where you can just brain dump and have it put tasks on your to-do list. It’s fine if you already know your task breakdown, but part of ADHD is not knowing or feeling overwhelmed by big tasks and needing them broken down to smaller components and I wish the AI assistant could help with that instead of making tasks for exactly what I say. For example, if I say “do laundry,” it just makes a task for that, but I wish it would break it out into components like “start a load of laundry,” “move it to the dryer to dry,” “take out and fold laundry,” and “put away folded laundry”. That might be a dumb example, but it illustrates what I’d like to see

I can’t delete lists on the desktop app, and the emojis glitch in the calendar day view, so it’s hard to see which part of the day you’re in.

I use this app a lot in both my personal and professional life because it makes it easy to see how the day is going and to move activities around. For work, though, it’s not ideal, because the Mac app is much weaker than the iPhone one. Because of that, I have to use the browser, and I can’t keep my work activities up to date easily. My job requires me to have hundreds of tabs open, so I lose track of the app’s tab and of what I need to do. Some days I end up going back to a notepad to remember my tasks, which defeats the main purpose of the app: helping people with ADHD.

Technically, on Mac it’s just one more app for listing tasks, not one that actually helps with ADHD.

reviews.title: What happened to the confetti???
reviews.text:
Update: one of the things I liked most about this app was the little celebratory confetti effect when I marked a task completed. It was an acknowledgment of effort and helped me stay motivated to keep working towards completing my tasks. Now it’s gone and Tiimo has gone from being genuinely useful to me, and being recommended to others by me, to something utilitarian that can easily be replaced with Apple’s built in reminders App. I’m very disappointed.

I’ve found this app to be helpful in keeping me focused on the things I want to accomplish. I know that it has more capability than I utilize, but I simply don’t need all of it. I do have one complaint and that’s with the frequent push for users to upgrade to premium. I’ve gotten pop ups every time I open the app this week encouraging me to take advantage of a premium subscription discount. It’s very frustrating to have my concentration disrupted by a sales pitch before I’m allowed to add a task. Now, with this most recent update, the option to choose an emoji symbol relevant to my task has been moved behind the premium pay wall. 

I understand that the developers are in business to turn a profit, but the tactic of gradually eliminating functionality feels disingenuous. If it continues, free account users will either feel forced to pay, or give up on the app altogether. I sincerely hope it won’t come to that for me.

reviews.title: Lots of wasted potential
reviews.text: I use AI to do my job, so the idea of this app as a light personal assistant seemed like a very useful application of the tech. In practice, this chat bot is really dumb and cannot actually parse a slightly nuanced todo or deal with a big brain dump. You also can only accept or reject its actions, you can’t correct them to tell the LLM what was wrong when the only issue is the time or a misheard word. For example, I said I needed to pick something up on the way home from an appointment, so it scheduled that reminder for 90min after the appointment ended instead of at the end time, but that was so many taps to correct it wasn’t really worth using the AI to begin with. It is not remotely capable of transforming a nebulous description of chores into actionable, scheduled steps, despite basically putting that ability on the tin. It’s really just a purpose built Siri focused only on reminders, and it can do a whole lot less than Siri. Add to that the UI is just plain confusing and unintuitive, things are divided into tabs in the most useless way, and none of the top level tabs feel as useful as they should be. This app feels like work to use when it’s supposed to make things easier.

reviews.title: I NEVER pay for apps but this was worth it!💜
reviews.text:
I NEVER write reviews. Like, EVER. But this app has helped me so much that I had to share it.
I have ADD and other executive functioning challenges, and scheduling has ALWAYS been something I struggled with. I’ve tried all kinds of scheduling apps, but I could never actually schedule in a way that works for me. It always felt like more work just trying to organize my life.
Then I found Tiimo. 🥹
The feature that completely changed the game for me is that I can voice-text my tasks, and Tiimo schedules them for me. I don’t have to sit there and manually enter everything, figure out where it should go, and spend forever organizing my day. I can basically just tell it what I need to do, and it helps me put it into a schedule.
At first, I thought this feature was free, but I eventually found out that I had to pay for it. 😕 As a college student who doesn’t have a lot of extra money—and someone who NEVER, EVER pays for apps—I was honestly pretty disappointed.
But I paid for it anyway.
And It was worth it.
The way this app works has genuinely made scheduling and keeping up with my responsibilities so much easier. I only wish the voice-to-schedule feature was free because I know there are SO many people who struggle with the exact same things I do who could benefit from it.
The basic functions of Tiimo are free, but the voice-to-text scheduling feature—which is the feature that helped me the most—requires a paid plan.
So if you struggle with scheduling, organization, executive functioning, or you’re neurodivergent, I 10/10 recommend giving Tiimo a try. ❤️
And Tiimo, THANK YOU for making something that actually works for people like me. 🙌
Now please make the voice scheduling feature free so more people can use it because I can’t.😭❤️

reviews.title: Updated review
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Tiimo for over a year now, and I have to say the updates since my last review have been really great. A lot of the things I mentioned before actually feel like they were taken into consideration.

What I love most is that the app keeps its simplicity, but still allows for creativity. I can customize my layout to fit my style without feeling overwhelmed by too many options. The built-in color schemes are vibrant without being “too much,” which makes it fun and motivating to use.

I especially appreciate how the day is divided into morning, day, and evening sections, which keeps things from feeling cluttered. The drop-down lists are another favorite—being able to expand or shorten them makes my schedule feel manageable.

One of the biggest highlights for me has been the new AI integration. I actually suggested this in my original review, so seeing it added was amazing! It’s still new and could be expanded, but it’s already a great feature that makes planning easier.

Since these updates, I’ve been using Tiimo more consistently, and I can honestly say it helps me stay on track throughout the day.

A few things I’d love to see in the future:
	•	More adaptations to the AI features.
	•	A true home screen view—being able to see tasks and check them off directly from my home screen without fully opening the app would be so helpful.
	•	A way to schedule travel time between activities, so that “empty space” actually reflects the time I spend driving or transitioning, not just free time.

Overall, Tiimo is still my favorite ADHD/autism-friendly planner. It’s colorful, simple, and motivating, and I can see it only getting better from here.

reviews.title: ADHD friendly claim is laughable
reviews.text:
Everything is focused on the AI agent instead of actually improving the app. Asking me to provide personal details of my daily life to a robot that will hold onto that info, learn from it, and distribute as needed must mean I’m no longer their customer. 

Routines are no longer a thing, you have to enter each task over and over again.

Calendar sync is PER DEVICE, not per account. I have everything synced on my phone, but the web and ipad apps don’t have those tasks listed without linking calendars to literally every place I could log in. I know it’s possible, Structured is able to do this. 
 
Editing the name of a task updates the icon/color, even when manually set. If you copy a task (because you have it set up how you like) and then edit ANY PART of the name, the icon changes. 

Also, speaking of icons, for calendar tasks, those come in per calendar and are uneditable. I totally get not being able to edit times, but how helpful is the icon/color if all of my work calendar items are pink🍖?

The ipad app isn’t responsive to different window sizes. I should be able to make the window phone sized to multitask while creating my todo list, but making it smaller makes all the text smaller. 

The watch app is absolutely useless imo. Yes, i can check things off, but most of the time I hit the wrong task. Why not create a complication that shows the current task and time (a la the iphone widgets). That nice picture of the watch on the website? Yeah, that’s not actually in the app. The best you’re gonna get is the live activity banner.

Tl;dr: most of their selling points either aren’t there, don’t work as well as they should (especially when you market to people with executive dysfunction!!), or are pretty much eliminated by all the AI functionality in the app.

Where it falls apart is reliability which is a pretty big deal if you had ADHD. I’m skeptical that it always alerts me as intended, but I can’t say for sure. 

The one I can pinpoint is that the calendar integration is buggy on the best days. Several times I’ve had to delete and reinstall the app to get my calendar events to populate in Tiimo. Or I have to wait 15+ minutes for it to pick up an event. The wait wouldn’t be such a big deal if it just worked consistently, but when I’m waiting to see if it’s working at all, that’s a huge pain.

There is also no way to search your tasks except for using the AI assistant which doesn’t really work. I’ve searched for past tasks by exact name to try to reschedule them and the AI assistant says they don’t exist. Then when I scroll for a few weeks, the task is there with the name I searched for.

It’s probably better for people who like to use the AI assistant to manage more of the scheduling for them, but if you just want a robust ADHD scheduler, I don’t think I’d recommend this one.

reviews.title: Great app, but family profiles need better options for integration
reviews.text:
Tiimo has been genuinely helpful for my own planning, and I appreciate how clean, focused, and easy it is to use. I also like that I can create multiple profiles for different family members. However, one feature that’s missing for me is a way for those profiles to be connected without being merged.

Right now, each profile is completely separate, so if I want to know what’s on my son’s schedule, I have to switch profiles. I’d love an option to layer other profiles’ events onto my own calendar while keeping them visually distinct.

Some ideas that would make this incredibly useful:

* Show other people’s events in a muted or grayed-out style (or with thinner event blocks) so they’re visible for awareness but don’t compete with my own schedule.
* Let users toggle which family members’ schedules appear.
* Allow a custom color for each person’s events so they’re easy to recognize at a glance.
* Keep ownership separate- the events would only be visible in my timeline, not something I can complete or manage. This would simply help me stay aware of my family’s day.

I’d also love a simple daily meal planning section. It doesn’t need recipes or nutrition tracking- just a small text field for breakfast, lunch, and dinner that’s tied to each day, and ideally could be shared across connected family profiles.

Tiimo is already a great app, and these kinds of family-awareness features would make it much more useful for households. I’d love to see this direction in the future.

There are three features tied for first place. 
- The first is a tiny detail on daily screen that tells me how much time I have between tasks. It has been the most liberating thing I did not understand  
I needed. Like most ADD sufferers if I have an activity planned I can do nothing except check the time until that event begins. This tiny feature means everything to me. It instantly relieves my anxiety because I no longer am constantly calibrating how much time I have before I need to get ready to go. Seriously, this is a ‘quality of daily life’ improvement.
 - Secondly, the AI piece.
You literally CAN empty your brain by speaking (no typing) of alllll the things you would love to get done so you can stop replaying them in your head for fear of forgetting the more random/potentially satisfying ones … And a list that you can check off is created FOR you. Dampens dread & overwhelm by 95%.
That’s a dream come true.
- Third, being able to see a larger version of your day/whole week, etc. in its entirety that’s now available to put on your desktop is like your fairy godmother creating a user-friendly spreadsheet. - I’m not saying there aren’t any learning curves, but it’s primarily about trading your habit of flying by the seat of your pants and hoping for the best w calm progress. 😑😂😉

reviews.title: Predatory “Get Pro” button
reviews.text:
Attempting to use the unpaid version of the app subjects the user to an animated “Get Pro” button on a 3 second animation loop. It sits at the top of the Todo and Reminder views and clicking on it once does not silence the animation. This is a predatory practice used in free to play mobile games and has no place in an app allegedly designed with neurodivergent users as a first class customer.

The presence of an attention hostile gimmick is immediately disqualifying, and only goes unnoticed by the broader community because the onboarding workflow conceals it. (require account to capture name and email address -> brief user relief to select desired workflows -> full screen Pro subscription upsell with trial -> “Buy Now” animation only gets observed if user didn’t avoided the trial)

Normally I would not ascribe this workflow to deliberate manipulation, but the fact that the Get Pro button never surfaced in my research indicates that it is either a new addition or has successfully prevented the majority of reviewers from observing it.

Hard pass from me. A company doesn’t get to claim best interests for the neurodivergent and then use this in their UI design. It’s twice damning because it means they know exactly what they are doing.

reviews.title: Update Suggestion
reviews.text:
I love this app. It has been one of the most helpful tools for keeping my day organized and keeping me on track when my mind would otherwise drift, especially on my phone where there are so many distractions.

One of the most useful features for me is the live countdown timer at the top of the iPhone screen. Having that timer constantly visible is honestly one of the biggest reasons the app helps me stay focused and follow through on what I planned for the day.

My main suggestions for a future update are about usability and staying on track throughout the day. First, when other Live Activities are also active, the smaller Tiimo Live Activity is mostly just an icon with a circular countdown bar around it. I think it would be much more helpful if the small Live Activity showed the actual time remaining in the center, with or without the circular bar around it. For me, seeing the actual timer is much more useful than just seeing a visual progress ring. The number gives a clearer sense of how much time is left and makes it easier to stay directed and intentional, especially near the end of a task. I’ve seen other apps implement this effectively, and it makes a big difference in staying aware of time and maintaining focus.

Second, I would really appreciate the ability to manually reorder tasks for the day without having to assign each one a specific time. Sometimes what is most helpful is not scheduling every task by the clock, but simply being able to set them in a clear sequence and work through them one by one. That takes away the mental burden of deciding what to do next and makes it much easier to stay on track.

Overall, I really love the app and appreciate how much it helps. These additions would make an already great app even better.

reviews.text:
I started using Tiimo because the AI assistant sounded like exactly what I needed. When it works, it’s genuinely helpful — it created manageable task steps and suggested ways to declutter my schedule. After a few good experiences, I was honestly ready to leave a glowing review.

Then today happened.

I asked the assistant to break a complex task into 10–15 minute steps spaced throughout my day so I could work in short bursts with breaks — a task the AI assistant is specifically designed and marketed to do.

Instead, the assistant repeatedly failed to recognize the task that already existed in my schedule, confused it with unrelated tasks, and kept asking for information I had already provided.

Even when it created subtasks, they were still much larger than the time blocks I requested. When I asked for smaller steps, the process repeatedly reset rather than refining the plan. At one point it even asked for an internal “activity ID,” which isn’t something a normal user would have.

What should have taken seconds turned into nearly an hour of trying to guide the AI through something it is specifically supposed to help with.

This issue appears reproducible when asking the assistant to break down an existing scheduled task into short time-blocked steps.

The core app itself seems thoughtfully designed, and the concept behind the AI assistant is excellent. But since the assistant is the main reason I tried the app, its unreliability is currently a deal-breaker.

If the AI becomes more consistent, Tiimo could easily be one of the best productivity apps out there.

reviews.title: Unfortunately not worth the freemium price
reviews.text:
I was originally very excited to discover this app — the accolades and hype made it appear to be the productivity and task tracking tool I had been searching for. At first, it does seem great — the core workflow of brain dumping tasks then scheduling feels very natural and smooth — but after just a few days the bugs and usability red flags begin to show. Below are some examples:

The freemium model is unnecessarily restrictive. With the free version you can create a task, but you need to pay $50+ a year if you want to edit that task.

The AI mode is borderline useless. You ask for help managing tasks and it will spit out a list of all of your tasks. I asked it to create a task called “call dentist office to schedule appointment” and had to go back and forth with the chat it because it ignored the ask and tried to actually create the appointment itself. It also isn’t clear from the chat output whether it actually adds something to your schedule or to your todo as you are always promoted to add a task after AI output..very confusing.

The focus mode is extremely buggy. There is no way to cancel a focus mode. If you have a scheduled task it automatically starts a focus state at that time and you can’t change that preference, which means anything you sync from your calendar or reminders will likely auto start and you will spend your time juggling pausing/unpausing or completing tasks and unchecking to get things to the correct state. You can drag the circle all the way around to complete a focus ring but you can’t drag it part of the way around to speed it up?

Tasks have focus rings but not sub tasks so managing time when there are many sub tasks is a fools errand. 

The best part of the app is what is offered for free. If basic free features weren’t gated by the freemium model, I could see the value in this app because aesthetically it’s probably the best one out there. If you strip away most of what is advertised as “pro” features (AI, lock screen live updates, widgets), I’d be happy with a todo + schedule and reminder notifications and would pay for a lesser subscription cost or lifetime fee.

reviews.title: Great interface, needs work
reviews.text:
The app is beautiful - good colors, organization, and satisfying UI. However the actual features need much improvement. I bought an annual sub of this app years ago, but it just wasn’t there yet. I came back for it today, just because I do miss the app and wanted to see how much has changed.

1) DRAG & DROP feature on timeline is janky. It is not intuitive. If I have a task scheduled for 4pm, and want to move a different task to right after it, nope. Whatever invisible timeline the spacing is set on is where the task will go. I could move the task after the 4pm one, but it will move to 2am or 3am. I need to keep pulling the task lower and lower, until the small times on left show the correct time, and it could be past 11pm tasks. It is confusing and does not make sense, and sometimes I forget what exact time I want it scheduled at, i just know i wanted it after my other scheduled task! 

2) Would also like a feature to drag duration of tasks, instead of needing to click into it and edit. Too time consuming.

3) What is the point of adding minutes focus time if it doesn’t shift the events after it? Let’s say i have a task with a 30 minute duration. I go over by 7 minutes. Now the rest of my schedule is messed up, obviously i cannot start on my next task if im still focusing on the current one, and i’ll get multiple notifications during my current one, alerting me of upcoming tasks or to start them, when I am 7 minutes behind!! it is overwhelming and ruins the purpose of the focus. They really need to create an automatic shift feature. 

4)  AI chat is useless right now, simply not there yet. I hate how it is at the bottom right, where the most useful button should be, and the new task feature is all the way on the top. Need to switch these two. 

I want this app to work well SOOO badly and have gone back and forth waiting for it to get where it needs to be, but I think this may be the last time I download if these features cannot be updated.

reviews.title: Maybe I missed something but…
reviews.text:
I am genuinely shocked by the effusive praise that the app has received. I downloaded it expecting something that would, at a minimum, feel useful. Yet, the app simply created additional friction in what could have been a great consolidator. The challenge is high, replace an ecosystem of time management and organizational apps. So, this should at the very least be as good as those other experiences. Additionally, it brands itself as particularly useful for people with ADHD — which I had been clinically diagnosed with, so it should be perfect, right? Wrong. Consider these three examples as how I knew the app wasn’t for me and that ultimately made it feel more gimmicky than actually useful:
1. I have a daily commute during which I regularly lose service. This also happens to be a great time to mess around with my schedule. For me, understanding context dependent patterns of behavior has been a huge win for helping me work with my sometimes floaty attention. The problem is, even basic things — like moving a past event/item from a previous day to the present day — cannot be done without an active internet connection.
2. I work Monday-Friday and thought it would be useful to have a high level to do list. Things like making the bed, reading a few times a week, exercise, and time to level up outside of work. Editing this schedule is incredibly tedious and requires repeated back and forth with the AI agent or manual editing of the schedule. When I took a week off of work to travel, or for Christmas a few weeks later, I should have been able to tell the agent to remove my tasks for those days. In the case of the former it repeatedly failed leaving me to do it manually. In the case of the latter it removed events on the wrong two days after confirming the correct days. I needed to manually shift over the events. Is there a universe where this just works? Sure. But my experience was that I wasted more time checking its work.
3. Remember that Christmas example from before? Well it turns out that somewhere in the process of rescheduling the time off to the correct days I managed to remove all subsequent occurrences of all my events/tasks. That would make it the second time I had to re-enter my entire schedule. Why manually? Because the agent is slow, imprecise, and inconsistent. It’s just faster to do it myself and to make tweaks with the agent, accept it’s not actually intelligent enough to understand and therefore not intelligent enough to manage my schedule/tasks. Occasionally it was brilliant, but more often than not it was a hassle to use. 

There are also subtle things like the way my tasks shift in importance and prominence throughout a day or week that make it feel less useful, especially because there’s a missed opportunity for 1) giving feedback about when you actually manage to finish things, 2) what you do and don’t finish, 3) meaningful capture and integration of your scheduling goals into your interactions with the agent, or 4) just finding ways to leverage research and other user experiences to give feedback or suggestions.

All in all, not a great user experience for me. It seems to be doing well with many others, but personally I found it was less efficient that just using my phone’s built in calendar and reminder system, which also works using “AI” voice controls. 

I would recommend more traditional methods of managing time for people with ADHD and to try this as an experiment, coming in with low expectations and allowing yourself to be surprised. 

It is not going to solve the more difficult problems of attention, motivation, energy, or time management. It may help but it may not. It seems, at best, a useful tool, given that you can find the right place for it in your toolkit. If you’re anything like me, it will eventually become a source of anxiety and annoyance as you learn to rely on it less and less. After a month or so of trying it out, it’s a no for me.

reviews.title: Solid base, but still needs a lot of UX improvements
reviews.text:
This app would be great, and I can see it becoming great in the long run if they act quickly to improve the UI/UX. 

First, it's laggy sometimes, specially when editing or creating tasks.

Second, there's no organized way to see all of the "routines" you created, they just show up on your daily view IF they're scheduled. I would think an app that creates routines would easily have a way to let me view and edit them all.

Third, given the way it's designed, it's a hassle to "schedule" your routines to a set time if they don't have a set beginning and ending time that remains the same everyday. I would think you would be able to just easily drag and drop an unscheduled/anytime routine into your calendar, but no, that is not possible, you have to edit it and go through a number of steps to accomplish that, and it's a dealbreaker for me.

Last but not least, even though you have created and set a routine for "morning", "afternoon" or "evening" to repeat daily or at a certain frequency, it doesn't make a difference, because it's always going to be bundled up with the rest of the "anytime" tasks.

Overall, the idea is great, and I really do believe they are targeting a market that is still searching for a better product, because there are many of apps like this out there, and none of them are a perfect fit. However, I'm not sure they are taking advantage of that gap properly. 

This apps feels like an early product of a startup, definitely not the first, but there are so many features that are super basic, crucial and intuitive that if they are not fixed and/or implemented soon, I'm unsure if they will actually end up standing out between the thousands of options out there.

I hope the developers can take this constructive feedback and improve the app as soon as possible to stay relevant in this crowded space. I hope to edit or change my review in the near future. For now, I will keep using reminders given the integration with all my Apple devices and everything.

Best of luck!

-Cannot control sequence of tasks within the Anytime, Morning, Daytime, Evening grouping

-Integration to calendar and other apps is just to import, it does not synchronize updates from Tiimo to other apps 

-Cannot control sequence of To Do items except for a random sequence within High, Medium, Low, unprioritized

-Help is non existent. The automated screen help without sound is a joke.
